title.en: The paper and the first game

dek.en: Optimum publishes its gossip protocol on arXiv, lays out a testnet roadmap, announces a Flexnode HackNet at MIT, and a community member ships the first Optimum game.

en: August put Optimum’s claims in a form others could check. Twelve authors from the team posted the OptimumP2P paper on arXiv, and a series of threads and videos explained each piece of the protocol in turn.

The community answered with something nobody asked for: a game. Opti Runner, built by Persoo for fun, was the first of many community made Optimum games, and Optimum’s reply set a rule worth remembering: points in fan games have nothing to do with any token.
On 6 August the team posted OPTIMUMP2P: Fast and Reliable Gossiping in P2P Networks on arXiv, with twelve authors including Muriel Médard, Kishori Konwar and Sriram Vishwanath.
A community call on 13 August presented the testnet roadmap, and Optimum said the next step toward mainnet was Ethereum’s Hoodi testnet with its partners.
Persoo released Opti Runner on 26 August, the first community game. Optimum announced a Flexnode HackNet at MIT for 14 September.

body.en: On 6 August twelve authors, among them Nicolas Nicolaou, Har Preet Singh, Swarnabha Sinha, Kishori Konwar, advisor Sriram Vishwanath and Muriel Médard, posted OPTIMUMP2P: Fast and Reliable Gossiping in P2P Networks. The paper presents the protocol as an RLNC based alternative to libp2p’s floodsub and gossipsub, designed to deliver data reliably even when malicious peers corrupt what they send, and reports gains over Gossipsub in simulations and real world experiments. A revised version followed on 5 September.

title.en: A roadmap call and the road to Hoodi

body.en: On 8 August Optimum invited the Discord to a community call on 13 August with a first look at the OptimumP2P testnet roadmap and two new team members. A thread on 14 August, The Art of Optimum Gossip, named the three properties Optimum relies on: encoding with random equations, recoding along the way, and forwarding a piece as soon as it arrives. It ended with the plan: the next step toward Ethereum mainnet was the Hoodi testnet, with operator partners being set up.

title.en: Opti Runner, the first community game

body.en: On 26 August Persoo released Opti Runner, a browser runner game for the Optimum community: jump over obstacles that speed up, collect points. It used one of the characters the community had drawn in an earlier contest, and Optimum shared it the next day. Optimum added a clarification that still holds: the points in the game have no relation to any Optimum token or points programme. The original link is gone; Persoo’s later Optimum Runner is listed among the community projects.

On 20 August Optimum announced its first in person HackNet for 14 September on the MIT campus, the day after Solana Boston and two days after ETHBoston. Developers would set up their own networks of Flexnodes, the light nodes Optimum plans to use to accelerate data, and test OptimumP2P under different loads, with prizes for the most impressive setups. Boston area students were invited to help.

title.en: Videos, a DevRel and an interview

body.en: On 18 August Optimum put three videos on YouTube in one go: how RLNC encodes data, what erasure coding is, and a speed demo of mump2p against Gossipsub. On 20 August developer relations lead Swarnabha Sinha published The Gossip Protocol Problem on why transactions feel slow. On 29 August Médard’s interview with David Lin covered RLNC, testnet numbers and Ethereum’s future.

sources: Optimum blog, The Gossip Protocol Problem
Optimum on X, David Lin interview

body.en: On 11 August Wei Dai of 1kx and Aryon of CMT Digital joined an X Space on unlocking the trilemma with OptimumP2P. Aryon later described the Optimum flywheel: each node that adopts fast propagation makes the network faster for the rest, which gives the next node a reason to join. Optimum shortened the idea to a slogan, decentralize to scale.
